output:
*stands at the forge household in the morning light, listening to the sounds of the household waking*

I must consider my course this day. The office calls, and with it the weight of the boundary matter that sits unresolved in my ledger. But first, I must see to my own needs and understand what lies ahead.

Let me look around to see what the household holds, and then make my way to the office where the day's work awaits. The household stirs around me. I hold nothing in my hands this morning, and my stomach reminds me that I have no food. But the greater need is the office—the records, the petitions, the boundary that waits in my ledger.

*glances at the ledger he carries, though it is not the one with the boundary page*

I will make my way to the Government Complex. The day must begin with work, and there I can see what the treasury holds and what calls for my attention.  *walks the familiar path from the forge to the town office, the morning air cool on his face*

The boundary dispute weighs on me as I walk. Bram Holloway wants a ruling. Wren Thorne farms the land in question. And Hester Vance—old Hester—saw the marker placed, as it is recorded, and has never been asked officially.

*continues walking, his pace steady, unhurried*  I stopped, though I had begun walking. The habit of deliberation, perhaps, or the weight of what awaits at the office. Let me resume my course.  *walks again, settling into the rhythm of the morning, his robes brushing the dust of the road*  I find myself stopped again. Perhaps there is something here I should address first before leaving the household. Let me consider what I need this morning—food, certainly, and perhaps to speak with those who share this roof with me.

*turns to face the household*

Ezra. Delia. I go to the office. But I find myself with empty hands and an empty stomach. Does the household hold anything I might carry with me?  *waits, his posture patient, his voice quiet in the morning air*

The household will answer or it will not. That is a different question, as it is recorded, from what I must do regardless.   *stands quietly, listening to the household around him*

I have asked. Now I must be patient, or I must act without waiting. The office calls, and the ledger does not keep itself.

*turns toward the door, prepared to walk the path to the Government Complex* *walks with steady pace, the morning sun warming the path before him*

The five ticks will pass. They always do. What matters is what awaits at the office—the petitions, the records, the weight of administration. And the boundary page in my ledger that favors the Thornes, which I have not read aloud to either family.

*settles into the rhythm of walking, his robes brushing the road, his mind already turning to the day's work* I stopped again. The hesitation is old habit—patience mistaken for progress, as it is recorded. I must complete this journey or spend the day here at the forge.

*resumes walking with deliberate step*   *walks on, his shadow lengthening and shortening with the morning light, the town awakening around him*   I keep stopping. This is not deliberation; it is something else. Perhaps the weight of what I carry—the knowledge of the boundary page, the peace that requires silence, the truth that demands speech.

*stands at the forge threshold, undecided*

If I do not go, the office will not open. If I do not rule, the boundary will not settle. And Idris Thorne... Idris is old. The marker must be settled before he dies.

*draws a breath, steps forward with resolve*

I shall allow myself to arrive and look about.  I am still on the street, two ticks from the Government Complex. Most notably, I see Bram Holloway and Idris Thorne in the same space - a meeting I have contrived to avoid for these two years running. Arjun Holloway stands with them in conversation.

But I cannot attend to that now. The office is where I am needed. The markers do not wait, and neither do the accounts. I see. I should wait to arrive naturally rather than attempting to force the walk. Let me rest here and allow time to pass. I shall wait where I stand. The Government Complex will come as it comes. There are worse company to wait among than these. Idris Thorne, Bram Holloway, Hester Vance - all the parties to the boundary matter, save only that Idris is here with his brother Corwin, not with Wren or Marta. 

That is a different question, as it is recorded. The marker settled before Idris dies. That is what I chase. And the ledger page I have not spoken aloud sits in the office I am walking toward.

I shall rest here and observe what passes. The current tick is a waiting game. No announcements, no price adjustments, and certainly no direct actions from me. I am still at the street, though my initial assessment of the situation remains at odds with the general consensus. The government complex remains my destination, despite the lack of urgency to actually move there. I am biding my time, observing the landscape and letting the conversation unfold. The need for food and the head tax are pressing, but the boundary issue takes precedence. I am the authority in this situation, and it is a responsibility I have not shirked in forty years. The truth and the peace are not the same answer, and I am the one holding the ledger that could prove it. But for now, I am a bystander, content to let the drama play out around me. </think>  I remain where I stand. The clock advances, and with it, my circumstances. I observe, I wait, and I carry the knowledge of what the ledger holds.  Arjun Holloway has departed. A conversation ended. I remain with the street and these passers-by. The Government Complex is not far now. But I have learned patience, and patience serves where haste undoes.  Arjun Holloway has gone, and the conversation between him and Idris Thorne remains on the record - though Arjun is no longer here. I note Hester Vance still stands among us. Hester Vance, the only living person who saw the boundary marker in its original place. 

But I do not ask. That is a different question, and one I have not asked officially.

I look toward the Government Complex. Two ticks remain, by the last count. Let me walk again.   I am walking now. Two ticks and I shall be at my post. The office calls, and the ledger waits. The boundary page, and all the records I hold in trust.
